title: Service-level Governance Ledger and Runway Simulator
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Teams lack a single, auditable ledger that translates service-level commitments (SLIs/SLOs) into initiative runway and de-escalation policies. As a result, engineers and PMs use ad-hoc spreadsheets to decide when to throttle rollouts or reallocate engineering bandwidth during sustained SLI degradation.

Goal: Build a Service-level Governance Ledger (SLG) that: (1) aggregates SLI targets and current burn rates per service, (2) maps initiatives to runway (how many days of safe operation remain), and (3) exposes a Runway Simulator to evaluate hypothetical mitigation plans (canary rollback, traffic shaping, priority throttles). The output should feed Console rollouts and the initiative prioritization engine.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: on-prem installation packaging and KMS-specific audit flows (handled in Private deployment EPIC).
tasks: Design ledger schema and mapping from SLI windows to initiative allocation
Implement backend aggregator service (read-only prototype) to pull SLI burn and uptime from telemetry
Expose a Runway Simulator UI component in Console with scenario playback
Integrate simulator recommendations with rollout throttle API (canary pause / rollback triggers)
Create a CSV/Confluence export for compliance and audit reviews
acceptance_criteria: Ledger stores per-service SLI target, rolling burn-rate, and linked initiative keys
Runway Simulator accepts a mitigation plan and outputs projected burn-rate reduction and estimated runway extension
Simulator UI shows confidence bands and a recommended mitigation (rollback/pause/traffic-shift) with rationale
Backend exposes an API endpoint used by Console route to fetch current runway metrics (latency < 200ms: 99.9% SLO example)
End-to-end demo with one real service (ingestion) and two synthetic scenarios completed and documented
